test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 09 March, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

Take your eye off the ball

options.text: To stop paying attention for a moment
Take an advice from a wrong person
Deteriorating and headed for complete disaster

solution:
Here the correct answer is **To stop paying attention for a moment.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom** "take your eye off the ball" **is often used in sports, particularly in games like cricket, baseball, and football, where the ball is the main focus of the game. It means to become distracted or lose focus on the task at hand, especially when it is important. 

 
 
• For example, if a cricket fielder takes his eye off the ball for a moment, he might miss a catch or let the ball go past him, resulting in a run for the opposing team. Similarly, in any other situation, if you take your eye off the ball, you might miss an important detail or make a mistake. 
 
 
 
• Hence, **option 1 - To stop paying attention for a moment **- is the correct answer as it best expresses the meaning of the idiom.
